strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: Addresses genuine GPU memory constraints preventing joint LiDAR-camera pre-training in fusion 3D perception
Comprehensive experimental work: Includes ablation studies, scaling property experiments across data regimes, cross-dataset evaluation on Once, and visualizations
Clear methodology: Well-written with proper technical formulations and implementation details
Consistent improvements on primary benchmark: 2.48% mAP gain over random initialization on NuScenes 5% fine-tuning setting
Solid presentation: Clear figures, good organization, and supplementary material
weaknesses: Limited novelty: All three main components are primarily borrowed/adapted from existing work (curvature sampling is straightforward derivative-based weighting; prototype learning directly adapted from SwAV; EM/Gram matrix regularization from SwAV)

Poor cross-dataset generalization: Only 0.53% improvement on Once dataset with 100% labeled data vs. 2.48% on NuScenes 5% data, suggesting method effectiveness is specific to few-shot NuScenes setting rather than general representation learning

Questionable curvature sampling approach: Computing curvature from a learned SDF that is poorly estimated early in training is circular reasoning; warm-up strategy appears ad-hoc; Figure 4 shows significant 'noisy estimation'; incremental empirical contribution (~1% gain in Table 3)

Insufficient prototype learning analysis: Claimed learning of 'objectness' and 'object parts' is unsupported; Figure 5 visualizations admit noise; no quantitative evaluation of what prototypes represent or comparison to semantic understanding

Limited experimental scope: Single main dataset (NuScenes), single downstream detector (BEVFusion), no comparison to other joint pre-training methods beyond UniPAD; missing comparisons to PONDER, MV-JAR, and other cited approaches
Missing memory analysis: No quantification of actual memory savings versus UniPAD; sampling numbers (NL=8192, NC=6144) appear large; no comparison to simpler memory-efficient techniques
Unclear mechanism: Ablation table shows incremental improvements (49.55→50.81→51.17) but doesn't isolate or demonstrate that improvements come from modality interaction vs. joint optimization
Overstated claims: '300% more improvement' in abstract is relative to small baseline (0.72%); absolute improvements are modest especially on realistic full-data settings
Reproducibility gaps: Code not provided; missing batch size, training time, GPU specifications; curvature estimation from neural field may be sensitive to implementation details

strengths: Addresses a practical problem: GPU memory constraints prevent joint pre-training of multi-modal 3D perception systems
Comprehensive experimental setup with careful control of training iterations to isolate pre-training benefits from convergence acceleration
Ablation study (Table 3) clearly demonstrates contribution of each component (joint pre-training, curvature sampling, prototype learning)
Scaling property analysis (Table 2) shows promise for low-data regimes with up to 7.22% mAP gain at 0.5% fine-tuning data
Cross-dataset transfer evaluation (Table 4) demonstrates some generalization to Once dataset
Clear presentation with helpful visualizations of curvature estimation and prototype assignments
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Curvature sampling is straightforward importance sampling; swapping prototype prediction is directly borrowed from SwAV [3]; EM optimization is standard. The contribution is primarily combinatorial

Curvature sampling lacks thorough justification: (1) Why is surface curvature the right informativeness metric? Flat surfaces (e.g., lane markings) could be important. (2) Figure 4 visualizations show significant noise in curvature estimation. (3) No comparison to alternative importance sampling strategies or ablation of sampling method

Misleading claims in abstract: '300% more improvement' is mathematically deceptive—this refers to 300% of UniPAD's 0.72% gain, not a 300% absolute improvement. Actual improvement is only 2.48% mAP. Scaling property claims refer only to reduced fine-tuning data, not actual dataset scaling

Limited evaluation scope: (1) Pre-training only on NuScenes; (2) Only BEVFusion downstream detector tested; (3) No comparison to other fusion pre-training methods (SimIPU [22], CALICO [41]) that are cited but not quantitatively compared; (4) Missing ablations on loss components separately (SwAV, EM, GMM individual contributions)

Prototype learning contribution is unclear: (1) Direct application of SwAV without significant adaptation; (2) Claims prototypes learn 'parts of objects' but visualizations (Figure 5) show road vs. vehicle assignments, not object parts; (3) Weak intuition for why swapping prototype prediction between LiDAR and camera features improves downstream detection

Missing critical analysis: (1) No GPU memory savings quantified—paper claims to address memory but provides no concrete numbers; (2) No computational cost comparison between CLAP and separate pre-training; (3) No analysis of which modality (camera/LiDAR) benefits more; (4) Warmup stage with uniform sampling (4 epochs) acknowledged as necessary due to noisy curvature estimation, but implications not explored

Weak baseline comparison: UniPAD is the only fusion pre-training baseline. Related fusion pre-training works [22, 41, 56] are cited but not included in comparison, limiting evidence that CLAP represents meaningful progress

Reproducibility concerns: Code not yet available; many hyperparameters to tune (8 loss weights); gaussian blur implementation for pixel weighting not clearly described; concrete batch sizes and GPU requirements during pre-training not specified

Sampling strategy seems extreme: Using only ~1% of points/pixels (sampling NL=8192 from ~100k points) risks losing important information. The claim that uniform sampling 'does not bring improvement' (Table 3) is insufficient justification that curvature is optimal

Incomplete experimental design: Table 3 shows uniform sampling only marginal decline (-0.26% mAP) from separate pre-training, yet this is dismissed without deeper investigation into why or whether other sampling strategies might work better

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses real GPU memory bottleneck preventing joint pre-training with clear articulation and concrete solution
Intuitive technical approach: curvature sampling is sensibly motivated (high-curvature regions like vehicles contain more information than flat road planes)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple metrics (mAP, NDS), object categories, ablation studies, scaling analysis, cross-dataset transfer, and informative visualizations
Consistent improvements: 2.48% mAP gain over random initialization with 1.76% NDS improvement across multiple object categories
Detailed reproducibility: extensive implementation details with specific hyperparameters and promised code release
weaknesses: Limited and questionable baseline comparison: UniPAD achieves only +0.72% (suspiciously weak for SOTA), and no comparison with other recent fusion pre-training methods (CALICO, SimIPU). The '300% improvement' claim misleadingly emphasizes modest absolute gains (2.48%)
Modest component contributions: Curvature Sampling alone provides +0.26 mAP and Prototype Learning +0.36 mAP—small gains for added complexity
Curvature Sampling limitations: acknowledged as noisy early in training (requires 4-epoch warmup), Figure 4 shows substantial estimation noise, and circular dependency on SDF prediction convergence

Insufficient prototype learning analysis: Figure 5 visualizations reveal substantial noise with many road points misassigned; no quantitative semantic quality metrics (e.g., IoU with ground-truth categories)
Limited experimental scope: only two datasets with degraded transfer performance (0.81% mAP on ONCE), single downstream detector per dataset, no evaluation on other fusion tasks

Technical clarity issues: EM formulation lacks clear justification for entropy minimization objective; gram matrix regularization borrowed from SwAV without 3D adaptation justification; convergence matching procedure informally defined
Overclaimed scaling property: Table 2 uses fixed pre-training with varying fine-tuning data (not true scaling study); extreme case shows poor absolute performance (23.71% mAP with 0.5% data)
Missing computational analysis: no runtime comparisons, memory usage, or efficiency metrics for curvature sampling computation

strengths: Addresses a real and important computational bottleneck in multimodal 3D pre-training that enables joint training of LiDAR and camera encoders for the first time
Strong experimental results with consistent improvements: 2.48% mAP on NuScenes (100% more than UniPAD), 1.28% on Waymo, and generalization to other datasets
Comprehensive experimental validation including ablations, visualizations, repeated evaluations, semantic segmentation results, and cross-dataset transfer
Geometrically intuitive curvature sampling strategy with supporting visualizations that effectively identifies informative regions
Clear presentation with good figures, logical flow, and sufficient implementation details provided
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: differentiable rendering from UniPAD, prototypes similar to SwAV; main contribution is curvature sampling and combination of components

Curvature sampling has fundamental limitations: circular dependency on SDF estimates being learned, persistent noise in early training requiring warmup period, no theoretical justification for geodesic curvature, no comparison with alternative sampling strategies

Prototype learning effectiveness inadequately demonstrated: visualization shows noisy assignments, unclear if prototypes capture semantic structure vs. local clustering, no ablation isolating EM/SwAV/GMM loss components individually, weak evidence for claimed 'modality interplay' benefits

Computational efficiency gains not rigorously demonstrated: no detailed runtime/memory comparison with UniPAD, training still requires 8 H100s, quantitative reduction vs. existing sampling methods not provided

Experimental concerns: unrealistic data regimes (5% NuScenes, 1% Waymo), small baseline improvement from pre-training (UniPAD only +1.12%), scaling property analysis conflates data efficiency with smaller baselines, missing statistical significance testing

Insufficient ablations and sensitivity analysis: no individual ablation of loss components, no analysis of hyperparameter sensitivity (NK, τ, loss weights), unclear contribution breakdown between joint training, curvature sampling, and prototype learning
Limited scope and generalization: only autonomous driving domain, smaller cross-dataset improvements suggest limited transfer, unclear applicability to other 3D perception tasks

Key technical details incomplete: appendix references marked with [?], Gaussian blur kernel size Kgaus not specified, EM formulation (Eq. 15) appears to be entropy minimization rather than standard EM

strengths: Addresses a real computational challenge in multi-modal 3D pre-training; prior work required separate per-modality training
Intuitive and practical curvature sampling strategy motivated by geometric observations about surface informativeness
Comprehensive experimental validation across two major datasets (NuScenes, Waymo) with multiple baselines and careful evaluation methodology
Well-designed ablation studies and supplementary experiments (semantic segmentation, repeated evaluation, cross-dataset transfer)
Rigorous experimental protocol avoiding convergence-only comparison (increases iterations until convergence for from-scratch models)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: curvature sampling is straightforward (||∇²_SDF|| as saliency); prototype learning heavily adapts SwAV without substantial innovation; differentiable rendering from prior work

Ablation study (Table 4) undermines main motivation: joint pre-training with uniform sampling (49.55%) is worse than separate training (49.81%), contradicting claimed modality complementarity benefits
Misleading performance claims: '100% more improvement' refers to relative change in gains, not absolute mAP improvement of only 1.36% over UniPAD

Curvature sampling has acknowledged instability (noisy in early epochs), requiring warmup workaround; visualizations show noisy estimations (Figure 4); no comparison with alternative sampling strategies

Prototype learning justification is weak: unclear why prototypes specifically benefit fusion perception; prototypes trained separately per modality; improvement of only 0.36% (50.81%→51.17%); visualization doesn't confirm semantic utility
Key ablation missing: Does joint training with curvature sampling (without prototypes) outperform separate pre-training? This comparison would isolate true joint pre-training benefit
~8-9 loss function hyperparameters (ωr, ωproto, ωsur, ωC, ωSwAV, ωEM, ωGMM, τ, etc.) without sensitivity analysis
Extreme few-shot setting (5% NuScenes, 1% Waymo) may not reflect practical scenarios; scaling experiments indirect (reduce fine-tuning data, not increase pre-training)
Limited generalization: cross-dataset transfer (Once) shows modest improvements; no comparison with other joint multi-modal pre-training approaches
Missing analysis: Why does joint + uniform sampling hurt? When does curvature sampling fail? How much computational overhead added by curvature estimation?

strengths: Clear problem formulation with practical motivation: addresses real GPU memory bottleneck in joint multimodal pre-training that existing methods like UniPAD cannot handle
Strong empirical results with proper experimental methodology: 2.48% mAP improvement on NuScenes with careful convergence control, and consistent gains across NuScenes, Waymo, and transfer tasks
Comprehensive experimental validation: multiple datasets, ablation studies, semantic segmentation tasks, cross-dataset transfer, repeated evaluations showing robustness (±0.1% std)
Technically sound approach: curvature sampling is intuitive and effective; each component (curvature, prototypes, EM, Gram regularization) shows clear ablation contribution
Good experimental design: avoids confounding convergence acceleration with pre-training benefits by controlling training iterations; scaling property exploration is insightful
weaknesses: Curvature sampling lacks rigorous theoretical justification: intuition that high-curvature regions contain more information is not formally validated; no analysis of when/why SDF second-order derivatives successfully identify task-relevant regions; 4-epoch warm-up with uniform sampling suggests instability without explanation

Unclear mechanism of fusion benefits: ablation shows joint+uniform sampling (49.55%) is worse than separate pre-training (49.81%), improvement comes primarily from curvature sampling and prototypes; limited evidence that learned representations actually capture complementary cross-modality information

Prototype learning design insufficiently justified: connection between prototypes and meaningful 3D scene parts is unclear; EM choice not compared to alternatives (k-means, contrastive clustering); number of prototypes (NK=512) appears arbitrary without sensitivity analysis; heavy reliance on SwAV framework with insufficient discussion of novel contributions

Many unjustified hyperparameters and design choices: 7 loss weights plus temperature, Gaussian blur kernel size, projection head architecture largely unspecified; no sensitivity analysis or ablation of these choices; no computational cost/training time comparison despite GPU memory being central motivation
Limited theoretical novelty: combines relatively straightforward geometric sampling with existing SwAV-style prototype learning; contributions feel incremental rather than conceptually novel

Evaluation scope limitations: experiments confined to autonomous driving datasets; 'scaling property' only explores reduced fine-tuning data not larger pre-training; main evaluation is 3D object detection only; no cross-domain generalization analysis

Technical clarity issues: some design choices seem ad-hoc (e.g., Gaussian blur for image pixel densification); missing details on projection heads and downstream fine-tuning; learning rate 0.00005 appears suspiciously small
